Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Merchant payments supported via mobile money and new interoperable rails (Visa Pay described as enabling consumers and businesses to pay/get paid across bank and mobile ecosystems; and national interbank platform planned to enable card/QR/instant services). Evidence supports at least partial digital P2B availability.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: Evidence indicates widespread mobile money ecosystems (e.g., M-Pesa, Airtel Money, Orange Money) and initiatives explicitly aiming at interoperability/instant transfers (interbank platform planned for Mar 2026; Visa Pay connects to mobile money). This supports existence of digital P2P transfers, but detailed national system documentation not consolidated in saved evidence.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: ATS/RTGS/ACH operational since 2017 (World Bank ICR); National Switch/Mosolo partially operational since Dec 2020 with 5 banks active/11 connected (not nationwide); interbank electronic payments platform planned end-Mar 2026 with instant transfers support. Partially deployed.
